title: Introduce tenancy-bounded GPU pools, IAM sharding modules, and VPC segmentation for private installs
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds modular Terraform for tenancy-bounded GPU nodepools, IAM sharding for least-privilege per-tenant roles, and optional VPC segmentation. Includes a migration helper for consolidating state into per-tenant tfstate backends. No user-visible API changes; operators should follow the migration steps in the PR description.
description: Summary: This PR introduces three coordinated Terraform modules and operational docs to support tenancy-bounded GPU pools, IAM sharding, and VPC segmentation for Redwood Private installations. Motivation: Private installs supporting multiple tenants have faced scaling limits and operational blast radius when GPU pools, IAM roles, and tfstate were global. This patch reduces cross-tenant coupling by enabling per-tenant GPU nodepools, tenant-scoped IAM role shards, and optional VPC network segmentation while keeping a migration path from the existing global layout. Changeset: 1) module/tenant-gpu-pool: new module to provision GPU nodepools scoped to a tenant identifier. Supports node taints/affinity, taints-per-profile mappings, and nodepool lifecycle policies. 2) module/iam-shard: decomposes previously-global instance roles into tenant-scoped IAM shards; includes minimal cross-tenant read-only roles for operator visibility. 3) module/vpc-segment: optional VPC segmentation helpers and route table templates to create tenant-isolated subnets and peering hooks for shared services. 4) state/layout: introduces per-tenant tfstate backends with a small migrator CLI (bin/tfstate-migrate.sh) and examples for locking and state naming conventions. 5) docs/migration.md: end-to-end operator guide for migrating from global state to per-tenant state with throttled rollout and rollback instructions. Compatibility: The modules are opt-in via feature flags in the installer config (installer.tfvars) so existing single-tenant installs are unchanged until operators enable tenancy mode. Migration plan: provide operator with a dry-run mode; run migrator for one tenant at a time; validate resources in a canary tenant and confirm monitoring/alerts before continuing. Rollout steps are included in docs/migration.md. Testing: added unit TF tests (kitchen/inspec-like harness) for module inputs and a small e2e run against a lightweight test VPC for GPU allocation behavior. CI: terraform fmt, validate, plan-for-check, and a batched apply smoke test in sandbox. Performance: GPU pool provisioning retains existing autoscaler hooks; no runtime-serving changes. Security: IAM shards follow least-privilege patterns and add a tenant-management role used by the installer controller; cross-tenant operator visibility is limited to a read-only audit role. Developer notes: the modules are parameterized to support both cloud and on-prem node discovery (kubelet registration or static node lists). Related: follows work called out in ENG-1289 and ties into the Dedicated autoscaler work. Checklist: [x] module unit tests added; [x] migration docs written; [x] e2e smoke; [x] CI green. Migration caveats: existing automation that assumes global role names must be updated; sample compatibility aliases are provided to ease transition.

review_thread: Rafael Ortiz (reviewer): Can we keep the old global role names as aliases around for 90 days to give automation time to switch?
Maya Chen (author): Added scripts/compatibility/role-aliases.tf that creates aliases for the previous role ARNs when feature flag 'enable_tenancy' is true. Documented the deprecation timeline.
Priya Nayar (reviewer): The migrator seems destructive if run without locking; can we add a dry-run and an explicit lock-check?
Maya Chen (author): Migrator updated to verify backend lock support and added --dry-run which produces a plan artifact. Also added retries and exponential backoff for state copy operations.
Samir Patel (reviewer): E2E smoke failed on first run due to subnet CIDR overlap in our sandbox; please guard peering creation with a cidr-check.
Maya Chen (author): Added cidr_overlap_precheck to vpc-segment and CI now runs the check before attempting peering.
notes: Operational impact: operators must opt-in to tenant mode and run the migrator for each tenant when ready. Backwards compatibility helpers included. Recommend rolling canary on a non-critical tenant first.
